label: prose:intro-beta-stability-closure
html: An isotope \mathcal{N}(Z, N) is \beta-stable if both its \beta^- and \beta^+ branching Q-values are negative, placing it at a discrete local minimum of the isobaric mass parabola. This section constructs the skein binding Lagrangian \mathcal{L}_{\mathrm{bind}}(Z, N; q) from the crossing-graded Wedderburn functional and proves that its discrete Euler–Lagrange stationarity locus defines the \beta-stability valley across the nuclear chart.
